items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: Yeah, the rehearsal for the Caravan. Was it the Caravan? Yeah, Mustard Van. Yeah. And we went up there, it was just Bob Mielke and myself, to talk over tunes we were going to do.

ctx.x: I know some pupils he had. No, there, there was just the one time when he said, this is the way you, you know, you're gonna, you're gonna play lead, you know, and, and you got to stomp off the tunes, and, uh, you know, and this is the way you, you beat your foot, you know. Mm-hmm. And, uh, he was trying to tell me how to run a band. Well, at the time I wasn't interested in learning how to run a band. I was interested in finding out what made him tick. Yeah. I mean, he was the guy that fascinated me, and I, and I…

Oh, you were talking about this rehearsal you were going to have? Yeah, the rehearsal for the Caravan. Was it the Caravan? Yeah, Mustard Van. Yeah. And we went up there, it was just Bob Mielke and myself, to talk over tunes we were going to do. And we were talking about Beale Street Blues, and Bunk sang a couple of the themes and got his horn out and played a few notes, I guess. And the next thing we knew, he was all sound asleep, and so we didn't know just what to do. We were kind of standing there, and so we…
It was probably later than the Freddie Moore, I think, anyway. I may have that documented someplace, too. But anyway...
